summary: SMTP module is mid-maturity: reliable T1 posture checks (open relay envelope test, VRFY/EXPN/RCPT user enum, STARTTLS/AUTH-before-TLS, weak/leaky SASL mechs, EXPN alias roster leak) and T0 version-gated CVEs for Exim (2019-10149, 21Nails, 2024-39929). No AUTH-attempt (spraying) or NTLM info-blob parsing (leaky mech is flagged but Type-2 not captured). Cross-transport wire records users into known_mail_accounts so imap/pop3 can spray them. Biggest gap: no offline crackable challenge capture (CRAM-MD5), no CVE probe (Exim 21Nails PoC) and no NTLM AV_PAIR harvest to feed known_hostnames.

findings.tier_evidence: Envelope-only MAIL FROM + RCPT to external recipient succeeded with no auth; a positive 250/251 rcpt code deterministically proves relaying is possible without ever calling DATA.
findings.promotion_notes: Send DATA with a self-addressed message to a controlled MX to prove end-to-end delivery; airgap-safe variant would need a controlled test recipient. Alternatively add a canary Message-Id-return-path probe.
findings.tester_next_step: swaks --server IP:PORT --from x@example.com --to your-test@controlled.tld --header 'Subject: recce-relay-canary' ; verify inbound at the collector. Or: nmap --script smtp-open-relay -p25 IP.

findings.tier_evidence: VRFY returning 250/252 is a deterministic user-existence oracle; probe only succeeds when the server honours VRFY.
findings.promotion_notes: Already covered by smtp_user_enum — VRFY alone stays T1 flag.

findings.tier_evidence: Concrete valid usernames extracted via VRFY/EXPN/RCPT differential; each name is a proven-existing local account that seeds cross-service spray (recorded into known_mail_accounts).
findings.promotion_notes: Feed enum'd users into imap/pop3 spray via known_mail_accounts (already wired) and into ssh known_users; a landed cred here becomes T3 initial access.
findings.tester_next_step: hydra -L users_from_recce.txt -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt imap://IP -t 4 -f ; also try pop3://IP and ssh://IP with same list

findings.tier_evidence: Enum-only: absence of STARTTLS in EHLO features — a fingerprint of posture, not a proven exploit.
findings.promotion_notes: Segment-sniffing to capture live credentials is out-of-band; not something recce can automate. Stays a posture finding.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -starttls smtp -connect IP:25 (expect connection refusal); tcpdump -A 'tcp port 25 and host IP' on a bridge to capture real client AUTH.

findings.tier_evidence: Observed AUTH mechs advertised in EHLO features while starttls missing — deterministic protocol misconfiguration (RFC 4954 §4 / RFC 6409 §4.3).
findings.promotion_notes: Actually attempt AUTH PLAIN with a canary credential — a 235 response confirms server accepts plaintext creds; requires a burnable account.
findings.tester_next_step: swaks --server IP:PORT --auth PLAIN --auth-user recce_canary --auth-password recce_pw ; a 535 processes the auth path (proves cleartext channel is live)

findings.title_pattern: SMTP AUTH offers deprecated challenge mechs
findings.tier_evidence: Mere presence of CRAM-MD5/DIGEST-MD5 in advertised mech list — fingerprint only; no captured challenge/response here.
findings.promotion_notes: Capture the server's CRAM-MD5 challenge (send AUTH CRAM-MD5 and read the '+ b64' continuation, then abort) — mirrors what imap.py / pop3.py already do. Provides hashcat-crackable material when a real client response is sniffed.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -starttls smtp -connect IP:PORT ; type: AUTH CRAM-MD5 ; base64-decode the challenge; sniff a real client's response and: hashcat -m 10200 challenge:response wordlist.txt

findings.tier_evidence: Detected via mere presence of NTLM/GSSAPI in AUTH mechs — the Type-2 blob itself is NOT parsed here (unlike pop3/telnet).
findings.promotion_notes: Send AUTH NTLM + a stock Type-1 blob (recce/ad/ntlm already has type1/parse_type2 as used by pop3.py); parse AV_PAIRs to recover NetBIOS/DNS computer, domain, forest. Feed known_hostnames/known_domains.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap -p25,587 --script smtp-ntlm-info IP ; the script's Target_Name and NetBIOS_Domain_Name are the AD-anchor for further pivot.

findings.tier_evidence: Version-gated banner match only; the CVE is claimed based on parsed Exim version < fixed-in, no actual exploit probe.
findings.promotion_notes: For CVE-2019-10149: send crafted RCPT TO:<attacker+${run{...}}@localhost> with the mail-injection primitive to prove command exec by triggering a DNS callback to a controlled sink. Highly destructive if fired against production Exim; must gate on RECCE_ACTIVE_ATTACKS.
findings.tester_next_step: For Exim < 4.92: use exim_4.87-4.91 metasploit module (exploit/unix/smtp/exim4_dovecot_exec) OR public CVE-2019-10149 PoC delivering an OAST callback (interact.sh). Confirm shell before running any secondary payload.

findings.title_pattern: SMTP EXPN alias expansion leaks user roster
findings.tier_evidence: EXPN 250 body actually parsed and member mailboxes extracted (multi-address roster returned) — a proven-exists roster, not just a fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain via known_mail_accounts into pop3/imap spray with common passwords; a hit is T3 mailbox access.
findings.tester_next_step: for a in all everyone staff wheel abuse ; do echo EXPN $a | nc IP 25 ; done ; feed harvest to hydra -L users.txt -P rockyou.txt imap://IP
